videos.title: Is American democracy safe? | Martin Wolf on the US midterms
videos.description:
As Americans prepare to vote in the November 3 midterm elections, FT chief economics commentator Martin Wolf asks what the result will mean for Donald Trump, the future of US democracy and America's place in the world. 

In the first of a six-part series of interviews with leading historians and political analysts, Martin speaks to the scholar and former Republican adviser Robert Kagan, who has spent a decade warning about Trump's authoritarian ambitions. 

They discuss how Trump has accumulated so much power, whether America's democratic institutions can still constrain him, and what might happen if Republicans lose control of Congress. Could these elections mark a turning point for American democracy or has the country already gone too far down the road towards authoritarianism?
 
To enjoy future episodes, be sure to subscribe to ‘Martin Wolf on the World’ wherever you get your podcasts. You can also watch Martin’s podcast series on the FT’s YouTube channel here: 

https://www.youtube.com/@FinancialTimes

videos.title: The Tiny Robot Solving a Massive Underground Crisis | WSJ
videos.description:
In January, a collapsed sewer pipe outside Washington, D.C., spilled more than 240 million gallons of raw sewage into the Potomac River. It is likely the largest sewage spill in U.S. history, but just one of an estimated 75,000 across the country each year, according to the EPA.

As aging sewer networks struggle with growing populations and changing weather patterns, a team of engineers and professors in Europe is developing a robot designed to detect and potentially address problems before disaster strikes.

WSJ explains how the $9 million EU-funded PIPEON project is tackling the dark and perilous world beneath our streets.

Chapters:
0:00 The sewage problem
1:06 Inside the robot project
2:04 The Potomac River disaster and impact
3:31 Mapping the networks
4:47 The tech and details of the robot
6:16 What's next?

WSJ Originals features in-depth reporting, investigations and on-the-ground journalism that uncovers the forces shaping business, politics and the world around us.

videos.title: The Space Force Showed Us Its Weapons Used in Iran and Venezuela | WSJ Equipped
videos.description:
An array of U.S. Space Force electromagnetic warfare systems are playing a key role in protecting American troops and degrading enemy satellites around the world. 

The Journal was granted rare access to a Space Force base in Colorado to learn how those systems work, and to speak exclusively with Guardians who flew them overseas to support operations in both Venezuela and Iran.

Hours after Tech. Sgt. Joshua Lomax jammed satellites to create a protective bubble around U.S. forces capturing Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro, he was given 72 hours to pack up his equipment and head to the Middle East, where the U.S. would soon launch its war against Iran. 

Chapters:
0:00 Space weapons
0:54 Spectrum warfare 
3:07 How the systems work
4:15 From Venezuela to Iran
5:32 Mission Delta 3

Equipped
Equipped examines military innovation and tactics emerging around the world, breaking down the tech behind the weaponry and its potential impact.

videos.title: How to Actually Fix the Colorado River Crisis | WSJ Pro Perfected
videos.description:
About 40 million people rely on the Colorado River. But an extended drought and a century-old legal framework have pushed the system to a breaking point. Now, a federal plan threatening deep cuts has ignited a fierce political and legal war across the Southwest.

WSJ spoke with Arizona State University water law professor Rhett Larson, who broke down where the government’s framework falls short, why easy fixes won't solve the issue, and what structural overhauls are needed to protect a crucial regional economy.

Chapters:
0:00 The Colorado River’s importance
1:00 The failing federal plan and the math problem 
4:21 Potential tech fixes and the economic problem
6:47 A full structural overhaul?
8:50 How Australia handled a shrinking river
10:05 The fight to keep the water flowing

Pro Perfected
Experts in engineering and design break down a ubiquitous problem, examining how the world is built and what can make it better.

#River #Water #WSJ
